title: Alquerque: Twelve and Twelve
tagline: Step. Jump. Capture.
description: An old board game of Spain and the Arab world, often described as a forerunner of draughts, made beautiful. Twelve pieces a side on a carved and inlaid board of 25 points joined by lines: step forward or sideways, jump to capture, and chain your jumps. Capturing is compulsory. Five opponent levels from Novice to Master, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, a short Learn course and Watch & Learn. Play in English, Spanish or Arabic. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has 12 pieces on a board of 25 points joined by lines. Light moves first, from the bottom, into the empty centre.
Step one point along a line, forward or sideways, never backward. Diagonal lines pass only through every other point.
Capture by jumping over an adjacent enemy piece into the empty point beyond, in any direction. Capturing is compulsory.
A piece that has jumped must keep jumping while it can, so one turn can take several pieces.
Capture every enemy piece, or leave the other side with no legal move. Think, Learn and Watch & Learn teach the ideas.

title: American Football: 7 on 7
tagline: Call the play, then play your position in seven-a-side football.
description: A simplified seven-on-seven game of American football in 3D. Pick a position, call plays and play it in real time: throw, run, catch, rush, cover and tackle. Five opponent levels, Watch & Learn, and a full Rules page.

title: Ampe
tagline: Clap. Jump. Throw a foot.
description: Ampe is a jumping and clapping game from Ghana, played in playgrounds across West Africa. Face your opponent, clap and jump on the beat, and throw out one foot: the same foot and the Leader scores, a different foot and the Follower does. Tap LEFT or RIGHT as the ring closes. Five computer opponents that learn your habits, a Learn path, Think hints, Practice and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: A steady beat runs. Each round is two beats: a clap and hop, then the big jump with a clap.
Tap LEFT or RIGHT as the ring reaches the gold target, when your player takes off.
At the top of the jump both players throw out the chosen foot.
Same foot: the Leader scores. Different feet: the Follower scores and becomes the Leader.
Be first to 11 points. The computer reads your habits, so mix your feet.

title: Baloot
tagline: The partnership card game of the Gulf
description: Baloot is the traditional four-player partnership card game of Saudi Arabia and the Gulf, related to the French game Belote. Bid for Sun (no trump) or Hokum (a trump suit where the Jack and 9 outrank the Ace), then play all eight tricks with your computer partner against two computer opponents. Ten hands-on lessons teach the whole game, four computer levels give you room to grow, and a new daily deal tests your reading of the table every day. Score only: no wagering, no ads, works offline. A full in-app Rules reference covers every ruling in detail.
howToPlay: New to Baloot? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every real move yourself.
TAP a card to raise it, TAP it again to play it, or DRAG it upward. TAP a big button to bid.
Bidding: one card is turned face up. Say Hokum (that suit is trump), Sun (no trump, x2), or Pass.
Follow suit. In Hokum, if you can't and an opponent is winning, you must trump the trick.
In Hokum the Jack and 9 of trump outrank even the Ace.
Declare runs, sets or Baloot (King and Queen of trump) in the first trick for bonus points.
Hint (3 a hand) suggests a play and explains why. Take back undoes your last move.
Race to 152 (or a shorter 61) with your computer partner against two computer opponents.

title: Bao la Kiswahili
tagline: The great board game of the Swahili coast
description: Bao la Kiswahili is the great strategy game of Zanzibar, Tanzania and Kenya, and the deepest of the mancala family. Bring seeds into play in namua, capture and sow from a kichwa, guard your nyumba, then fight the mtaji. Six lessons, Watch & Learn, Think hints, four computer levels and a full illustrated Rules page.
howToPlay: You sit at the bottom. The two rows nearest you are yours; the glowing pits are the ones you may play.
Namua: you start with 22 seeds in your store. Each turn one goes into a pit of your front row.
If a glowing pit faces enemy seeds you must capture: tap it, then choose the end of your front row (kichwa) to sow the captured seeds from.
If nothing can capture, play a takata: pick a glowing pit and a direction. Both directions show where the sowing would end.
Mtaji: once your store is empty, sow a pit with 2 or more seeds. If its last seed lands on a pit facing enemy seeds, you capture.
Win by leaving your opponent with an empty front row or no pit that can be sown.
Think shows a good move and why. Undo takes a move back. Watch & Learn plays a whole game for you to study.
The Rules page explains every rule, nyumba, safari and kutakatia included, with pictures and text up to 300%.

title: Basketball 3x3
tagline: Pick a role. Screen, drive, shoot, rebound.
description: Play real 3x3 half-court basketball in 3D: pick guard, wing or big, and control that one player while the computer plays your two teammates and three opponents. Time your shot in the green zone, set screens, pass to the open player, steal, block and rebound. Five opponent levels, a Learn path, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Choose a role: guard, wing or big. You control that one player.
Left thumb moves. SHOOT: hold and release in the green zone. PASS to a teammate, CROSS to beat a defender.
Without the ball: CALL for a pass, hold SCREEN to free a teammate, CUT into space.
On defence: stay between your man and the hoop, STEAL when the ball is low, BLOCK a shooter, JUMP for rebounds.
First to 21 or the lead at 10:00 wins; overtime is first to 2.

title: Big Card Solitaire
tagline: Huge cards, tap to play, every deal winnable.
description: Big Card Solitaire is Klondike redrawn for comfort: oversized high-contrast cards, tap-to-move instead of dragging, and no timers or flashing effects. Every deal is checked so it can actually be won. A built-in "what can I do?" hint highlights your legal moves whenever you're unsure. An in-app Rules page explains every move in plain language.
howToPlay: Tap a card to select it, then tap where you want it to go - if only one move is legal, it plays automatically.
Build the four foundation piles up by suit, from Ace to King.
Stack tableau cards down in alternating colours.
Tap the stock pile to draw a new card when you're stuck.
Tap "what can I do?" any time to see every legal move highlighted.
Open Options any time to change the table colour, card back, 2- or 4-colour suits and motion. Your choices are remembered.

title: Carrom
tagline: Flick, pocket, cover the queen
description: Carrom is the flick-and-pocket board game played across South Asia, in homes, clubs and tournaments. Slide your striker along the baseline, pull back to aim and let go: coins slide, rebound off the cushions and drop into the corner pockets. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, play the computer at four levels or a friend on one phone, and try a new trick shot every day. A polished plywood board, glossy coins and a dotted aim guide that shows where each shot will go. Large text, reduced motion and left-handed layout included. An in-app Game Rules page covers every edge case. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: eight short lessons where you make every shot yourself.
DRAG the striker sideways along your baseline to place it. It turns red if it touches a coin.
DRAG BACK from the striker to aim. The dotted line shows the shot; a longer pull is a harder flick. RELEASE to flick.
Pocket a coin of your colour and you shoot again. Pocket nothing, or the other colour, and the turn passes.
Pocket the red queen, then pocket one of your own coins on the same or the next stroke to cover it, or she goes back.
Foul: if the striker falls into a pocket, one of your pocketed coins goes back to the centre and the turn passes.
Clear your coins first to win the board: 1 point for each coin left on the other side, plus 3 for the covered queen.
Keyboard: Left and Right slide, A and D aim, Up and Down set power, Space flicks. Hint shows a good shot.

title: Chess
tagline: The timeless game of sixty-four squares.
description: A complete, beautifully carved chess set: full rules including castling, en passant and promotion - with a full in-app rules reference for every piece and every way to win or draw - six AI levels from Beginner to Grandmaster, a 12-lesson tutorial, and a two-game AI vs AI demo to watch and learn from. Three original board themes with dimensional, carved-look pieces. Free to play, forever. No ads, no purchases.
howToPlay: TAP a piece to see its legal moves highlighted, then TAP a lit square to move it.
Or DRAG a piece to its destination and let go - both work everywhere.
Castle by TAPping or DRAGging the king two squares toward a rook.
Promote a pawn on the last rank by choosing Queen, Rook, Bishop or Knight in the picker.
Play White, Black, or pass-and-play Two Players on one device.
Choose an AI level from Beginner to Grandmaster, and use Undo or a Hint if you get stuck.
Learn the rules and basic tactics in 12 hands-on lessons.
Watch two full AI vs AI games play out end to end from the title screen.

title: Chogan
tagline: Ride, swing and score in the ancient game that became polo.
description: Chogan is the ancient mounted game of Iran and the ancestor of polo. Take one of three riders, steer a galloping horse, time your mallet swing and drive the ball between the posts. Five computer rival teams, a Learn path, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Drag with your left thumb to ride; push to the edge to sprint.
Hold SWING to wind up and let go to hit; steer to choose the direction.
Get the ball beside your horse (the ring turns green) before you swing.
Press HOOK to knock away a rival's mallet as he winds up.
Play four short periods; the team with more goals wins.

title: Congklak
tagline: The shell game of Southeast Asia
description: Congklak (Congkak in Malaysia, Sungka in the Philippines) is the carved-boat mancala of Southeast Asia: seven houses a side, seven shells in each, both players sowing at once to open. Sow one shell at a time, scoop on when you land on a full house, shoot the house opposite when you land in an empty one, and play again when you end in your storehouse. Nine hands-on lessons, five computer levels, a daily puzzle and pass-and-play. Burnt houses raise the stakes each round. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a glowing house in your right-hand column to sow it. TAP anywhere while shells move to fast-forward.
Shells go one to each place ahead, into your storehouse but never your opponent's.
Last shell in your storehouse: play again. In a full house: scoop it up and keep sowing.
Last shell in your own empty house: shoot, taking every shell in the house opposite.
Each round starts with both players sowing at the same moment.
A round ends when the player to move has no shells; houses that cannot be refilled are burnt shut.
Undo takes back a move; Hint (3 per game) shows a good move and why.

title: Cornhole
tagline: Pitch bags at the slanted board and sink them in the hole.
description: The backyard bag toss. Pull back and let go: land a bag on the slanted board for one point or in the hole for three, and push your rival's bags out of the way. Real board size and slope, soft fabric bags with a flip and a flop, cancellation scoring, five computer opponents, Think, Learn and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Press on the lawn, pull back and to a side, let go to throw.
Pick Slide, Arc or Flip and add spin to curve a slide.
Bag on the board: 1 point. Bag in the hole: 3.
After four bags each, only the difference counts. First to 11 or 21 wins.
Tap Think for a throw that was tested with twelve simulated bags.

title: Disc Flick Table
tagline: Flick it. Ring it. Pocket the twenty.
description: A Canadian tabletop classic with real disc physics. Pull back and flick across a maple board, bounce off brass pegs, drop one in the pocket for 20, and outplay five rivals.
howToPlay: Slide your disc along your line, then pull back anywhere like a slingshot and let go.
Pull length sets the power and pull direction sets the aim.
If a rival disc is on the board, your flick must touch one or it is removed.
Rings score 5, 10 and 15 and the centre pocket scores 20.
Eight discs each per round; the higher total after the last round wins.

title: Crown Fields
tagline: One crown per row, column and region. No touching.
description: Crown Fields is a calm grid-placement puzzle: place one crown in every row, column and coloured region so that no two crowns touch, even diagonally. Every puzzle is generated fresh with exactly one solution, solvable by pure logic. Play a quick 7x7, take on the tougher 10x10 Expert board, or try the Daily Puzzle. A free Hint and Undo are always there if you get stuck. An in-app Rules page explains every mechanic. No timers, no pressure - just clean logic.
howToPlay: Tap a cell to cycle it: empty, then crossed out, then a crown.
Placing a crown automatically crosses out every cell it would make illegal.
Every row, column and coloured region needs exactly one crown.
No two crowns may touch, even diagonally.
Fill the whole board correctly to solve the puzzle.
Stuck? Tap Hint for a free crown placement, or Undo to take back your last move.
Choose Play 7x7 or Expert 10x10 from the title screen, or try the Daily Puzzle.
Tap Colours on the title screen or while playing to change the region colours - your choice is remembered.

title: Stone and Sweep
tagline: Throw it. Curl it. Sweep it home.
description: Slide granite stones down a sheet of pebbled ice with real friction, curl and collisions. Place the broom, choose the weight and the turn, then rub the ice to sweep: the stone slides further and curls less. Play five computer rivals, share the phone, learn the shots in short lessons, or watch two players explain their choices.
howToPlay: Drag on the ice to put the broom where the stone should stop.
Choose Draw, Tap, Takeout or Peel, and an in-turn or out-turn curl, then press Throw.
Rub the ice while the stone slides: sweeping carries it further and keeps it straighter.
After the last stone, the side closest to the button scores one point for each stone closer than the other side's best.
The side that scores gives up the last stone for the next end.

title: Diketo: Stones
tagline: Toss one, take the rest, catch it before it falls.
description: The traditional Southern African stone-toss game on a swept dirt yard. Take the pile out of the hole and back in, stage by stage, with a timed toss and catch. Five computer levels, pass and play, lessons and Watch & Learn.
genre: stone toss and pick-up skill game
howToPlay: Hold the pad to set the toss height, release to toss.
While the stone is in the air, tap or drag across the stones to take.
Tap CATCH when the ring closes on the landing spot.
Move the pile out of the hole and back in, stage by stage.
Drop it and the turn passes: the first to finish the last stage wins.

title: Dominó Cubano: Doble Nueve
tagline: Cuban partnership dominoes. Read the table, trust your partner.
description: Real Cuban partnership dominoes with the full double-nine set, played the way it's played in Miami's Domino Park and across the Caribbean. Your AI partner actually reads the table: every pass proves what a seat doesn't hold. Three difficulty tiers put that to real use, up to full Torneo partnership reading. No chips, no stakes - first team to 100 wins.
howToPlay: You and the seat across from you are partners against the other two - ten tiles each, fifteen stay asleep.
Drag a tile from your rack onto either glowing end of the line - it plays if either number matches.
No match? Tap Pass - the game only lets you pass when you truly have nothing to play.
Every pass is a clue: it proves that seat holds nothing matching either open end, for the rest of the hand.
A hand ends when someone empties their rack, or all four seats pass in a row - lowest pips wins the block.
First team to 100 points wins the match. Choose Casual, Club or Torneo difficulty before you deal in.

title: Dudo: Andean Bluff Dice
tagline: Hide your dice. Bid. Bluff. Call it.
description: The bluffing dice game of the Andes, made beautiful: five dice under a leather cup, woven tables, bone dice that tumble and shine. Bid on what lies under every cup, call Dudo when you smell a bluff, or risk an exact Calzo. Five computer levels, two to four friends on one phone with a screen that hides the dice, Think with the exact odds in plain words, six short lessons and Watch & Learn with every cup open. Play in English or in Spanish. No timers, no ads, nothing wagered.
howToPlay: Everyone has five dice hidden under a cup. Look at your own dice, then bid on how many of one face lie under all the cups together.
Pick a face, set the number and tap Bid. A bid must go up: more dice, or the same number of a higher face. Ones, called pacos, are wild.
Too high? Tap Dudo! Cups are lifted and counted and the loser gives up a die. Sure it is exact? Tap Calzo: win a die back, or lose one.
Think tells you in plain words how many matching dice to expect and how likely the bid is. The last player with a die wins.
Pass the phone with friends: a screen hides the dice between turns. Learn and Watch & Learn teach the game.

title: Durak
tagline: The card game of the fool
description: Durak, widely regarded as the most played card game of Russia and its neighbours: attack, defend, throw in, and try not to be the last one holding cards. Play against one to three computer players in Podkidnoy or Perevodnoy, learn in eight short lessons, solve a daily endgame and read the story of the game. A full in-app Rules reference covers every mechanic. Offline, score-only, no wagers.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: eight short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a card to lift it, TAP it again to play it. Or DRAG it onto the table.
Beat an attack with a higher card of the same suit, or with a trump.
TAP Take to pick up the table when you cannot or will not beat.
Throw in cards whose rank is already on the table; TAP Bito when done.
Refill to six from the stock. The last player holding cards is the fool.
Hint (3 a match) shows a good move and why. Undo takes back your last move.
Daily Deal: both hands face up. Only one first move keeps you safe; find it, then play on.

title: Fanorona: Approach & Withdraw
tagline: Madagascar's national board game: capture by approach, capture by withdrawal.
description: Fanorona is the strategy board game of Madagascar: 22 stones a side on a board of 45 points, where you capture whole lines by moving toward them or away from them, then chain on along new lines. Play six computer levels from Beginner to Master, learn in eight short lessons, watch two computers play with a think-and-reveal commentary, or share one phone. Full rules inside, large text, no ads.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn: eight short lessons where you make every move yourself.
Tap a stone, then a lit point. The number shows how many stones that step captures.
Approach: step toward an enemy line and capture it. Withdraw: step away and capture the line behind you.
If a step can do both, you choose. Gold is approach, blue is withdraw.
Capturing is compulsory. After a capture your stone may keep going along a new line, or you can end the turn.
Think shows a strong move with numbered arrows. Danger rings the stones you could lose next turn.
Watch & Learn plays a whole game between two computers: guess the move, then see it revealed.
Win by capturing every enemy stone. Twenty turns with no capture is a draw.

title: Football: Seven a Side
tagline: One role. One team. A real match.
description: Seven-a-side football in real-time 3D. Pick a role (striker, winger, midfielder, defender or goalkeeper), play it with a thumb stick and context buttons, and let the computer play the rest. Five rival levels, Learn drills, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Pick one role before the match and keep it.
Drag the left thumb to move; hold SPRINT to run.
With the ball: SHOOT (hold, release), PASS, LOB or THROUGH.
Without it: TACKLE, SLIDE, HEAD or CALL; goalkeepers swipe to dive.
Win two halves of 2, 3 or 5 minutes.

title: Footy: Kick and Mark
tagline: Kick, mark and tackle: six-a-side on a whole oval.
description: A simplified original take on the Australian football tradition, in real 3D. Pick one player, handball and kick to your forwards, win the mark, tackle cleanly and score through the four posts. Five computer levels, a Learn path with a tutorial for every role, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Drag the left stick to run; hold RUN to sprint.
KICK or HANDBALL to a teammate: push the stick towards him and follow the teal ring.
Run to the gold ring and press MARK a third of a second before the ball arrives.
After a mark, press KICK when the bar is in the middle.
TACKLE the carrier from behind; score 6 for a goal, 1 for a behind.

title: Fox and Geese
tagline: One fox. A flock of geese. A cross of frost.
description: Fox and Geese is the classic hunt game, played on a cross of 33 points across Europe for centuries. One fox faces thirteen geese: the geese step forward or sideways and never back, and try to close the fox in; the fox slips between them and jumps any goose left alone, chaining jumps in one turn. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play either side against four computer levels or a friend on one phone, choose a flock of 7 to 17 geese, and solve a new puzzle every day. Hand-painted fox and geese on a moonlit board. An in-app Rules page covers it all. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
The geese move first. Tap a goose (its points glow), then tap where it steps: one point forward or sideways, never backward.
The fox steps one point up, down, left or right, or jumps over a goose to the empty point behind it and captures it.
After a jump the fox may jump again in the same turn: tap a red point to go on, or tap the fox or Stop here to end its turn.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
The geese win when the fox cannot move. The fox wins when only 5 geese are left. The same position three times is a draw.
Warnings mark geese the fox could take next. Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
Choose a flock of 7 to 17 geese (13 is classic). Beat each level with each side for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for everyone.

title: Gabata: Three-Row Sowing
tagline: The three-row sowing game of Ethiopia and Eritrea.
description: A carved wooden board of eighteen holes: sow seeds round your own loop, relay through full holes and capture a whole column when your last seed drops into an empty hole. Five opponent levels, two players on one phone, Think with a reason in words, six lessons and Watch & Learn. Play in English or choose the Amharic option for the menus and scores. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Tap one of your holes that holds seeds. All its seeds are dropped one by one into the next holes of your loop.
If your last seed lands in a hole that already holds seeds, pick those up and sow on.
If your last seed lands in an empty hole, you capture every opponent seed in that column.
The game ends when a player runs out of seeds. Captured seeds plus the seeds in your own holes are your score.
Think shows the best move and why.

title: Go
tagline: The game of stones and territory
description: Go is the classic board game of East Asia: Weiqi in China, Baduk in Korea, Igo in Japan. Place stones on a kaya-wood board, surround territory and capture what has no liberties. Learn in eleven hands-on lessons, play the computer at four levels on 9x9, 13x13 or 19x19 boards, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a new puzzle every day. Dead stones are found for you, every refused move is explained, and hints say why a move is good. Hand-painted board, slate and shell stones, large text and reduced motion. An in-app Rules page covers every rule in exact detail. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: eleven short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a crossing to aim: a ghost stone appears. TAP it again (or press Place) to play. DRAG to slide the ghost.
A stone or group with no empty neighbours (liberties) is captured. Playing where a stone would have none is not allowed.
Ko: you may not retake a single stone straight away. A move can never repeat an earlier whole-board position.
Pass when nothing useful is left. Two passes in a row end the game and the board is counted.
Scoring: your stones plus the empty points only you surround. White gets komi: 5.5 on 9x9, 7.5 on larger boards.
Dead stones are found for you: tap a group to change your mind, then Accept. Hint suggests a move and says why.
Four computer levels, three board sizes, two players on one phone, and a new daily puzzle with a streak.

title: The Road to Lanka
tagline: An exiled prince. A stolen princess. A leap across the sea.
description: A retelling of the Ramayana, the great Sanskrit epic, as thirteen playable scenes with painted, hand-crafted characters lit like a stage. Draw the great bow at Janakpur, walk out of Ayodhya, defend the forest home at Panchavati, rally the vanara army, fly with Hanuman across the sea, slip through Lanka by night, build the bridge, command the war and face the ten-crowned king. Then carry the lamps home to Ayodhya. Every character and scene is drawn in code, with real story and heritage notes throughout. A Chapter Guide (title screen and pause menu) explains how every chapter is won.
howToPlay: Each chapter opens with a story card, then a short demo shows the exact commands. Replay it any time from the card or the pause menu.
TAP: touch once. HOLD: keep your finger down. DRAG: slide it. RELEASE: lift it. Every chapter tells you which command it needs.
The bow: HOLD 1 to 2 seconds, then RELEASE inside the gold band. The exile: HOLD to walk, RELEASE beside the people with lamps.
Forest, deer, allies, night roofs and bridge: TAP the target you choose. Never TAP the deer or birds in the forest.
Hanuman's flight and the chariot home: HOLD and DRAG up or down to steer. Lift your finger to fly level.
The war: TAP a unit card, then TAP a lane. The duel: DRAG back, line up the dotted arc, RELEASE to shoot.
The fortress run: TAP to leap, HOLD for a higher leap. Open Controls on the title screen for every command.
Earn up to three stars per chapter and follow the road from Janakpur to Ayodhya. Open The Story & Its World for notes on the epic.

title: Gonggi: Five Stones
tagline: Toss one, take the rest, catch it before it falls.
description: The traditional Korean five-stones game on a patchwork mat. Plan the route, set the toss, and climb from one at a time to kkeokki. Five computer levels, pass and play, lessons and Watch & Learn. Play in English or Korean.
genre: five-stones toss and catch skill game
howToPlay: Scatter the stones and tap the one to hold.
Tap the stones to take, in order, without touching others.
Hold the pad to set the toss height, release to toss.
Tap when the ring closes to catch the falling stone.
Finish with kkeokki: catch all five on the back of your hand.

title: Tower of Hanoi
tagline: Move the tower. Find the pattern.
description: The classic disc-stacking puzzle, made to feel wonderful: lit, lacquered discs on carved pegs that lift, slide and drop with a satisfying thud. Three chapters from 3 to 10 discs, a four-peg variant and scrambled starts, a Daily Challenge, and a real solver behind Think and Watch & Learn so every level shows its exact minimum. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Move the whole tower of discs from the first peg to the gold peg, one disc at a time.
Tap a peg to lift its top disc, then tap the peg where it should go. Or drag the disc and let go.
A larger disc may never rest on a smaller one. Such a move is refused and does not count.
Every level shows its minimum number of moves. Three stars for matching it.
Think shows the best next move from wherever you are. Undo takes a move back.
Watch & Learn plays whole towers with the best moves, with time to think and a Pause button.

title: Hare and Hounds
tagline: One hare. Three hounds. One narrow board.
description: Hare and Hounds is a traditional hunt game for two sides on a tiny board of eleven points. Three hounds close in on one hare, but hounds may never move backward, so every step is a promise. Trap the hare before the hunt clock runs out, or slip past the hounds. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play either side at four computer levels, take on a twelve-level campaign with stars, solve a new puzzle every day, or play a friend on one phone. Hand-painted animals, large text and reduced motion. An in-app Rules page covers it all. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
One hare against three hounds. Tap a piece (its legal points glow), then tap where it goes. One step along a line per turn.
Hounds win by leaving the hare no move. They never capture, and may never move backward, only forward or sideways.
The hare wins by getting past all three hounds, or by lasting until the hunt clock (the hounds' moves) runs out.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Hare's reach shows where the hare could step next. Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
The campaign has twelve hunts: fewer moves earn more stars. The daily puzzle is the same for all, longer on weekends.
Beat each level with each side for a star. Winning unlocks new boards and a snowy set of pieces.

title: Golden Sling
tagline: Pull, aim, release. Guard the harvest.
description: A hand-carved slingshot, a golden field, and birds raiding the crop. Pull back, aim and release to scare them off before the harvest is gone. Every bird behaves differently, the wind picks up as you advance, and every miss sends the flock scattering. Free to play, with a new Daily Hunt every day. An in-app Rules page covers every bird and mechanic.
howToPlay: Drag back from the slingshot to aim - the dotted arc shows where the stone starts to fly.
Release to fire. Pull farther for more power; gravity and wind bend the shot.
Hit birds to scare them off and score. Hits in a row build a combo multiplier.
A miss costs the stone and startles nearby birds, so pick your shots.
Never hit the owl - it is protected and costs you stones.
Reach the level's quota before your stones or the crop runs out.

title: Huarong Dao: Sliding Puzzle
tagline: Free the commander. Fewest moves wins.
description: The classic Chinese sliding-block puzzle, made to feel wonderful. Slide carved lacquer blocks around the pass to lead Cao Cao to the gate. 32 layouts including the famous Heng Dao Li Ma, the fewest possible moves for each, a real hint, unlimited undo and Watch & Learn, which solves levels step by step. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Lead Cao Cao, the big red block, to the gate at the bottom of the board.
Drag a block into an empty space. It slides along the real route and never through other blocks.
Or tap a block to see every cell it can reach, then tap one.
A move is one block set down on a new cell, however far it travels.
Think shows the best next move; press it again to make it. Undo takes back a move.
Finish close to the fewest possible moves for three stars. Solve six levels in a chapter to open the next.
Watch & Learn solves levels for you, step by step, with time to think.

title: Hurling: Sliotar Dash
tagline: Strike, solo and score.
description: The fast Gaelic field game of Ireland in 3D: pick a role, strike for a point or a goal, rise the ball, solo run and hook. Five opponents, Learn drills, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Pick a role: forward, midfielder, back or goalkeeper.
Drag the stick to run; push all the way to sprint.
RISE picks the ball up; PASS hand-passes; HOOK checks a rival.
Hold STRIKE: release in the GOAL zone (3) or the POINT zone (1).
Tap Think for the best play and why.

title: Jack and Boule
tagline: Read the gravel. Point, shoot, win the end.
description: Pétanque from Provence with real rolling physics. Slingshot your steel boule toward the jack across generated gravel pitches, choose to point or shoot, and outplay five rivals.
howToPlay: Pull back on the screen like a slingshot, then let go to throw.
Pull length sets the distance and pull direction sets the aim.
Choose Roll, Half-lob, Lob or Shoot, and add backspin to stop short.
Read the slopes, sand and stones: the gravel decides where a boule stops.
The side with the closest boule scores. First to 13 wins.

title: Kabaddi: Raid and Tag
tagline: Raid, tag and tackle in 3D.
description: The traditional South Asian team sport of raid and tag: choose your approach, tag defenders, and get home before the chain closes. Five opponents, Learn lessons, Think hints and Two Players.
howToPlay: Pick a move: step in, feint, touch, bonus line or retreat.
Cross the baulk line before you can go home.
Tap as the ring closes for the best timing.
Defend with holds, blocks and dashes.
Tap Think for the best move and why.

title: Kegeln
tagline: Nine pins, a heavy ball and a long wooden lane.
description: German-heritage nine-pin skittles with real pin physics. Plan your aim, hook and weight, flick the ball up the lane and clear the pins in Volle and Abräumen.
howToPlay: Drag on the lane to place the aim ring; drag the ball to choose where you start.
Pick a hook (seven curves) and a weight (Soft, Medium, Firm).
Flick the ball up the lane or tap Roll, and watch the pins fall.
Volle: every throw at nine pins. Abräumen: clear the pins you left.
Tap Think for a line that was tested with twelve simulated rolls.

title: Ken and Ball
tagline: A string, a heavy ball and a steady hand.
description: A Japanese skill toy with real string physics. Drag the ken, pop the ball and land it in a cup or on the spike, climb 20 tricks, or chase a Combo Run.
howToPlay: Press and drag to move the ken like a hand.
Pull up quickly or hold Pop and let go to send the ball flying.
Slide a cup under the ball and move down with it as it lands.
Put the spike under the ball with the hole facing it to spike it.
Flip the ken for the base cup. Fewer drops earn more stars.

title: Kilikiti
tagline: A village match: swipe, flick, run and catch.
description: Samoa's own bat-and-ball game in a modern, simplified take for your phone. Pick one role in your team (batter, bowler, inner or deep fielder) and play it while the computer plays everyone else. A three-sided bat, a hard rubber ball and a big fielding side, in short matches with real runs, fours, sixes and run outs. Five opponent levels, a Learn path for each role, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Pick one role in your team. The computer plays everyone else.
Batter: swipe the way you want the ball to go as it reaches the bat; tap RUN after a hit.
Bowler: pick a swerve, then flick up the screen. The ring shows where it lands.
Fielder: hold a finger to run, tap just as the ball reaches you, then choose where to throw.
Tap ? for a hint with a reason, or watch the computer play and explain in Watch & Learn.

title: Tafl
tagline: The king's table of the North
description: Tafl is Hnefatafl, the Viking-age strategy game of Northern Europe. A king and his twelve defenders, surrounded by twenty-four attackers, must break out to any corner of the board before the ring closes or the king is taken. Play Copenhagen 11x11, the modern standard board, or start on the smaller, quicker Brandubh 7x7. Learn in ten hands-on lessons where you make every move yourself, play either side against four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new proven puzzle every day. Carved oak board, bone and horn pieces, hearth light, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a piece (its reachable squares glow), then TAP a square to move. Or DRAG and drop.
Every piece slides like a rook: any distance in a straight line, never jumping.
Trap an enemy piece between two of yours in a line to capture it. Moving in between two enemies is always safe.
The defenders' king reaches any corner to win. The attackers win by taking the king or ringing in every defender.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Warnings show the king's open lines to a corner. Hint gives a good move and why (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
Beat each level with each side, on both boards, for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for everyone; keep a streak.

title: Kite Duel
tagline: Read the wind. Cross the string. Cut them loose.
description: A fighting-kite duel in a living sky. Touch to steer, choose slack, steady or pull, and saw through your rival's string before yours parts. Five rivals, four skies, real wind and string tension.
howToPlay: Touch the sky to set your kite's heading.
Choose Slack, Steady or Pull for the string.
Read the wind strip: pull in lulls, ease off before gusts.
Swing across your rival's string and keep it tight to cut.
Win two rounds out of three.

title: Kolam
tagline: One line. Every dot.
description: A calm drawing puzzle inspired by the South Indian kolam tradition: trace one unbroken glowing line around every dot and close it. 72 patterns on square, diamond and staggered grids, Think with checked reasons, Watch & Learn, a daily pattern and a free-draw Sandbox with mirror symmetry. No timer, no ads.
howToPlay: Touch near a dot and drag around it; the line follows your finger.
Between dots choose how the line passes: wrap, cross or dip.
Marks on gaps are fixed. Draw one closed line through every arc that keeps them.
Guide warns before a turn that would trap part of the pattern; Think explains the next stretch.
Three stars: close the loop, no Think, no wrong turns.

title: Konane
tagline: The jumping game of Hawaii
description: Konane is a traditional Hawaiian strategy game: black and white stones fill a carved lava-stone slab, and every move is a jump that removes the stone you hop over. Whoever cannot jump loses. Learn with eight hands-on lessons, watch a full free Auto Play demonstration that thinks, reveals and plays every move for you, play a computer at four levels on 6x6, 8x8 or 10x10 boards, or solve a new daily puzzle where exactly one first jump wins by force. A full in-app Rules page covers the opening, the jump and how the game is won.
howToPlay: TAP one of your stones, then TAP a glowing square to jump there.
Jump over a touching enemy stone into the empty square behind it.
Keep hopping in one straight line, or stop after any hop.
You cannot turn a corner in one move, and you must jump if you can.
The first player with no jump left loses. There are no draws.
Eight lessons teach every rule by doing, or watch free Auto Play think and play a full game for you.
Take back moves and ask for hints that explain why.
Solve the daily puzzle: only one first jump wins.

title: Kubb
tagline: Knock the blocks, throw them back, topple the king.
description: The Nordic lawn game with real wooden physics. Drag back to throw a spinning baton, knock over the other team's kubbs, throw your own fallen ones back as field kubbs, and fell the king last to win.
howToPlay: Drag back on the pitch like a slingshot and let go to throw a baton.
Pick Loft (Low, Medium, High) and Spin to change how the baton flies and lands.
Knock down field kubbs first, then the baseline kubbs, then the king.
Fallen kubbs are thrown back into the other half: drag a ring, let go.
Topple the king too early and you lose. Tap Think for a tested throw.

title: Ludus Latrunculorum
tagline: Slide. Sandwich. Enclose the dux.
description: The Roman game of little soldiers on a marble board with pieces of bone and glass. Slide your soldiers like rooks, sandwich the other side's soldiers to take them, and enclose the enemy dux. A reconstructed game, with five opponent levels from Novice to Master, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, a short Learn course and Watch & Learn. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has 15 soldiers and a dux. Ivory moves first. Slide one piece a turn along its row or column over empty squares, like a rook.
Sandwich an enemy soldier between two of your pieces, in a row or column, to take it. Moving between two enemies is safe.
A soldier on an edge falls only along the edge; a corner soldier falls to the two squares beside it.
The dux cannot be sandwiched: enclose it, every side held by you or the edge, and you win. No move left, or only a dux left, loses.
Think shows a good move and why; Learn and Watch & Learn teach the ideas.

title: Lotería Cantada
tagline: Sung riddles, folk-art cards, and a bean on every tabla.
description: Mexican picture bingo with an all-original deck. A caller sings a rhyming riddle for each card, you tap the picture on your tabla and shout ¡Lotería! when your pattern is complete. Play the computer, face to face with a friend, or call a real table.
howToPlay: Choose a tabla: a grid of 16 pictures.
Listen to the riddle and tap the matching picture to drop a bean.
Each call stays open only for a moment, so be quick.
Press ¡LOTERÍA! when your pattern is complete, before the computer does.
Use Hint, or Watch & Learn to see a whole round explained.

title: Mahjong
tagline: The game of the four winds
description: Mahjong is the four-player tile game of China, played around the world. Build four sets and a pair before three computer players do: draw, discard, and call chows, pungs and kongs. Hong Kong-style scoring shows exactly which patterns scored and why. Learn in eleven hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole hand face-up for you, play three computer levels, get plain-words hints, and solve a new discard puzzle every day. Thick ivory-and-jade tiles, a felt table, large text, reduced motion and three tile-face styles. Play in 中文 or English. Score only, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eleven short lessons teach every step, or watch free Auto Play play a whole hand face-up for you.
Each turn you draw a tile and discard one. TAP a tile to lift it, then TAP it again (or DRAG it up) to discard.
Build four sets and a pair: a chow is three in a row in one suit, a pung is three alike, a kong is four alike.
When another player discards a tile you can use, TAP Chow, Pung, Kong or Win!, or TAP Pass. A short timer runs; you can turn it off.
Win! beats Pung and Kong, which beat Chow. A chow may only be taken from the player before you.
A win needs at least 1 fan (or 3 in Settings). The score screen shows each pattern and why it scored.
Tap Why? for advice on your discard. The daily challenge is three puzzles, the same for everyone.
Play a Quick hand or a whole East round of four deals. Your hand is saved when you leave.

title: Makruk: Thai Chess
tagline: The chess of Thailand, with a tutor beside you.
description: Makruk is Thailand's traditional chess: cowrie-shell pawns, a queen that steps one square, and endgames played against a count. Play five computer levels from Beginner to Master, learn in eight short lessons, watch two computers play with a think-and-reveal commentary, or share one phone. Think shows a strong move and why, and a live Count strip teaches the counting rules. Full rules inside, large text, no ads.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn: eight short lessons where you make every move yourself.
Tap a piece, then a lit square, or drag it. Dots are quiet moves and red rings are captures.
Checkmate the other Khun to win. Gold moves first.
A Bia (cowrie) steps forward and captures diagonally. On the sixth rank it becomes a Bia-ngai.
When no Bia remain the counting rule starts. The Count strip shows the count, the limit and the moves left.
Think shows a strong move and the reason. Threats rings your pieces that could be taken next.
Watch & Learn plays a whole game between two computers: guess the move, then see it revealed. Pause any time.

title: Matkot Beach Rally
tagline: The beach paddle game from Israel. Keep the ball alive.
description: Matkot, the wooden-paddle rally heard on every Israeli beach. Drag to run, lift to swing, and rally with a partner for the longest streak or beat five rivals who read the ball like real people. Golden-hour sand, sea and a sky that slides toward sunset.
howToPlay: Press anywhere and drag to run. Lift your thumb to swing.
Get under the white ring on the sand: that is where the ball drops.
Meet the ball on the left or right of your paddle to aim left or right.
Swing early for a fast smash, late for a high lob; mid-height is sweet.
Beach Rally: keep it going with Dana. Match: first to 7 or 11 wins.

title: Nine Men's Morris
tagline: The mill game of Europe
description: Nine Men's Morris, known as Muhle in Germany, Moulin in France and Merels in England, is a medieval mill game carved into cloister seats across Europe. Place nine men on a 24-point board, slide them along the lines and take an enemy man with every row of three. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, watch a free Auto Play demonstration play a whole game for you, play five computer levels from Apprentice to Grandmaster, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a mill puzzle every day. Every rule is written out in full on the in-app Rules page. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Ten short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you.
Placing: Light starts. Tap an empty point to place a man. Each side places nine.
Sliding: tap a man, then a glowing point beside it (or drag it there). Men slide one step along a line.
Three men in a row is a mill. Tap a glowing red enemy man to take it. Men in a mill are safe unless all enemy men are in mills.
Down to three men? You fly: any man may jump to any empty point.
You win when the enemy has two men left or cannot move. Same position 3 times, or 50 moves each with no mill, is a draw.
A refused move shows a red ring and says why. Hint (3 per game) explains a good move. Undo takes back.
Five levels, a daily mill puzzle, boards and men to earn. Large text and calm (reduced motion) options.

title: Snakes & Ladders Cloth Board
tagline: The painted-cloth dice race, reimagined.
description: The classic dice race on a hand-painted cloth board in the Indian tradition. Roll, hop, climb ladders named for good habits and slide down serpents named for slips. Flick the die across the table and watch it tumble. Play one die or pick the better of two each turn, add extra rules (exact finish, six rolls again, bump back), and choose the classic board, a fresh fair board, or the board of the day. Play 2 to 4 people on one phone or against computers, ask for hints, read the full rules, or Watch & Learn as the computer plays a whole game. Text size up to 300%.
howToPlay: Tap Roll, or flick the die across the table, to throw it.
Your pawn hops forward that many squares along the zig-zag numbers.
End on the foot of a ladder to climb it; end on a serpent's head to slide down.
In Pick of Two mode, tap the die you want to use, or tap its glowing landing square.
Tap Hint any time to see what lies ahead or which die is better, and why.
Reach square 100 first to win. By default you need the exact number to finish.
Choose extra rules in the setup: exact finish, six rolls again, bump back.
Play 2 to 4 people on one phone, or against computers from Easy to Sharp.
Watch & Learn plays a whole game by itself so you can see how it thinks.

title: Morabaraba
tagline: The game of twelve cows
description: Morabaraba is a traditional board game of Southern Africa, played in Lesotho, South Africa, Botswana and Zimbabwe. Twelve cows each on a board of three squares joined by lines and diagonals: place your herd, form a mill of three to shoot an opposing cow, slide to open and close mills, and fly when you are down to three. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, watch a free Auto Play demonstration play a whole game for you, play four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a daily puzzle. Painted dusk-over-the-veld art, large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
Placing: TAP an empty point to place a cow. Each side places all twelve cows first.
Three cows in a line make a mill, diagonals included. Close one and TAP a glowing cow to shoot it.
A cow standing in a mill is protected, unless all of that side's cows are in mills.
Sliding: TAP a cow, then a glowing point (or DRAG it). Cows move one step along a line.
Down to three cows you may FLY a cow to any empty point. Fewer than three, or no move, loses.
Illegal move? The cow tries, comes back, and a message says why. Hints explain themselves.
Beat each computer level with each colour for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for all.
Auto Play (free, silent): watch a full game play itself - it pauses for you to think, then reveals and plays the move it chose.

title: Mū Tōrere
tagline: The eight-pointed star game of Aotearoa
description: Mū Tōrere is a traditional Māori board game of Aotearoa New Zealand. Four stones each sit on an eight-pointed star around a central pit, the putahi: slide one stone at a time and leave your opponent with no move. The game is tiny and fully solved, all traps and foresight. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you, climb a Ladder of twelve opponents, solve a new proven puzzle daily, or play a friend on one phone. Carved-wood board, shell and greenstone stones, calm sound. An in-app Rules page spells out every move. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eight short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you.
TAP one of your stones (its legal points glow), then TAP a point. Or DRAG the stone there.
A stone moves one step: to the next point around the star, or between the rim and the putahi (centre).
A stone may enter the putahi only when it stands beside an enemy stone. From the putahi it may step to any empty point.
You win when your opponent has no legal move. The same position three times is a draw.
Move not allowed? The stone tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Hint shows a good move and why (3 per game). Take back undoes your move and the reply.
Climb the Ladder of 12 opponents. The last two cannot be beaten, only held to a draw.

title: Nonogram
tagline: Fill the grid. Reveal the picture.
description: A calm logic picture puzzle: use the numbers beside the grid to decide which squares are filled and a small illustration appears. 121 pictures from 5 by 5 to 20 by 20, each with exactly one solution that logic alone can reach. Think explains the next step in plain words, Watch & Learn solves pictures with the reasons shown, and a daily picture keeps it fresh. English and Japanese. No timer, no ads.
howToPlay: The numbers beside each row and above each column give the lengths of the runs of filled squares in that line.
Tap a square to fill it, or drag along a line to fill a run. Use Cross to mark squares you know are empty.
Think finds the next square that logic proves and explains why. Use Zoom and Move on big boards.
Every picture earns up to three stars: solved, no Think, no wrong marks.
Learn and Watch & Learn teach overlap, edges and gaps step by step.

title: Noughts & Crosses
tagline: Three in a row, made deep.
description: The classic three-in-a-row game, made beautiful: lit bronze crosses and verdigris noughts on carved marble, with four ways to play. Classic 3x3, the Roman Terni Lapilli with sliding pieces, Misère where three in a row loses, and a 4x4 Quad board. Five opponent levels up to a solver that never slips, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, eleven lessons and Watch & Learn. No timers and no ads.
genre: abstract strategy, three in a row
howToPlay: Take turns with your opponent placing your mark. X always goes first. Three in a row wins.
Tap an empty square to place your mark. A full board with no line is a draw.
Terni Lapilli: place three pieces each, then tap a piece and a joined empty point to slide it. Diagonals count.
Misère: complete three in a row and you lose. Quad: four in a row, or a 2x2 square, wins on the 4x4 board.
Think shows the best move and why: this blocks a fork, this wins. Undo takes a move back.
Learn teaches threats, blocks and forks in eleven short lessons. Watch & Learn plays whole games with time to think and a Pause button.

title: O An Quan: Mandarin Squares
tagline: Vietnam's pebble game of sowing and capture.
description: The traditional Vietnamese children's game, rebuilt on a lacquered wooden board: sow stones one at a time, relay through full squares, leap an empty square to capture and win the two mandarins. Five opponent levels, two players on one phone, Think with a reason in words, six lessons and Watch & Learn. Play in English or in Vietnamese. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Tap one of your squares that holds stones, then choose Sow left or Sow right (or swipe from the square).
Your stones are dropped one by one. If the last one lands before a full square, pick that square up and sow on.
If the last stone is followed by an empty square and then a full one, you capture the full one. Chains count.
The two big mandarin stones are worth 10 points each. The game ends when both are captured; the higher total wins.
Run out of stones and you refill your side from your winnings. Think shows the best move and why.

title: Oche Darts 501
tagline: Hold steady, release, and check out on a double.
description: Pub darts with a drifting aim point that tightens then tires. Race down from 501 with a proper double-out, learn finishes with the checkout coach, and play five opponents or a friend.
howToPlay: Touch and hold to aim: the aim point sways, then settles, then tires.
Let go while the aim point is over your target.
Three darts a visit; each dart is subtracted from 501.
Finish exactly on zero with a double, or you bust.
Tap Think for the best next dart and checkout route.

title: Okey Offline
tagline: Turkey's tile rummy, four at the table.
description: Okey is the tile rummy game of Turkey. You and three computer players share 106 tiles; each deal a turned-up indicator decides which tile is the wild okey for that deal only. Draw, arrange your two-row rack into runs and sets (or seven pairs) by dragging, then finish by discarding your last tile. Finish on the okey itself and the deal counts double. Sort helpers tidy the rack, a free Hint explains its reasoning, and Watch & Learn plays a whole deal with time to think before each move. Three computer levels, a full Rules page, English or Turkish labels. Offline, no ads, score only.
howToPlay: Four players, 106 tiles. A turned-up indicator makes the next tile up in that colour the wild okey for this deal.
Your turn: DRAW from the face-down stack, or TAP the glowing pile on your left to take your neighbour's last discard.
ARRANGE your rack by DRAGGING tiles between its two rows. A green line shows every valid run or set.
Runs are 3+ consecutive tiles of one colour (12-13-1 is allowed). Sets are 3 or 4 tiles of one number in different colours.
DISCARD one tile: drag it onto your own pile, or tap it and press Discard.
Finish when the 14 tiles you keep are all in runs and sets, or form seven pairs. Finishing on the okey doubles the deal.
Runs, Sets and Smart sort the rack for you. Hint is free and explains its choice.
Watch & Learn plays a whole deal for you with time to think before each move, and a Pause that freezes it any moment.

title: One Arrow Oath
tagline: Nothing fires twice.
description: A deckbuilder where your best cards can be played only once. You are an archer sworn never to loose the same arrow twice: every named Arrow you play is spent for the whole run, so each fight asks how little you can afford to spend. Read every enemy's intent, answer it with the right element, take on Debts that come due at the worst moment, and decide whether to keep the Covenant or break it. Inspired by a warrior's vow from ancient Sanskrit epic poetry, one of the world's oldest literary traditions. The world and every name in it are original. An in-app Rules page covers every system.
howToPlay: Read the intent above each enemy: what it will do this turn, and which element answers it.
Press a card and pull it down like a bowstring, then release to play it. Tapping it twice also works.
Gold-framed Arrows hit hard and are spent for the whole run. Steel-framed Techniques come back.
Answer an attack with the element that beats it. A Ward cancels it; a matching Arrow also strikes for +50%.
Finish weak enemies with Reed Shafts. Never loose a named Arrow at a Lure - it will be wasted.
After each fight, take one new card. Camps heal, the Tuner trades, Envoys offer choices.
Debts give power now and come due in the final fight. Settle them at a Camp if you can.
Breaking the Covenant wins the moment, but Standing lost that way is hard to earn back.
New to it all? Tap Auto Play on the title screen to watch a whole run play itself, at a thinking pace you choose.

title: Oware
tagline: The seed-sowing game of West Africa
description: Oware is the classic seed-sowing game of Ghana and West Africa, part of the mancala family. Twelve pits, forty-eight seeds: lift a pit, sow seeds round the board, and capture pits that end with two or three. Learn in eight short hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace, play the computer at five levels from Easy to Grandmaster, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a new capture puzzle every day. Hand-carved wood and glossy seed art, large text and reduced motion. Full rules are in the in-app Rules page. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eight short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP one of your pits on the bottom row to sow it. Glowing pits are the ones you can play.
Seeds go one per pit, counter-clockwise: along your row, then back along your opponent's row.
If your last seed makes an opponent pit hold 2 or 3, you capture it, and the pits before it if they also hold 2 or 3.
A pit with 12 or more seeds laps the board and skips its own pit.
If your opponent has no seeds you must play a move that gives them some.
First to capture 25 seeds wins. Undo takes back a move; Hint (3 per game) shows a good move and why.
Daily puzzle: TAP the one pit that captures the most seeds. Same puzzle for everyone.

title: Pachisi
tagline: The royal race of the cross
description: Pachisi is the royal race game of India, ancestor of Ludo. Throw six cowrie shells, count the mouths that face up, and race four pawns around the embroidered cloth cross to its centre. Land on a rival to send it home, hide on the marked squares, block the way with a pair. Play the full game or the friendly Ludo mode, with two to four players, against four computer personalities or friends passing one phone. Nine hands-on lessons, Auto Play (a full game plays itself at a pace you set), a daily race and an exhaustive in-app Rules reference. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP the cowries, or SWIPE up across them, to throw. Count the mouths facing up: 1 up = 10, 2 = 2, 3 = 3, 4 = 4, 5 = 25, 6 = 6, none = 12.
Grace throws (10, 25, 6, 12) give another throw and are the only throws that let a waiting pawn enter the board.
Pawns that can move glow. TAP one to see where it lands, then TAP it again to move it. A pawn that cannot move shakes and tells you why.
Race anticlockwise once around the cross, then up the middle lane to the centre. The centre needs an exact count.
Land exactly on a rival pawn to send it home. Squares marked with an X are safe; two of your pawns on one square form a block.
Play 2, 3 or 4 players against computers (Beginner, Cautious, Balanced, Bold) or pass one phone between friends.
Ludo mode uses one die and a smaller board. The daily race sets the same six throws for everybody.

title: Parqués: Salida y Cárcel
tagline: Colombian parqués: break out of jail, split your dice, capture rivals
description: Colombia's version of the pachisi family. Free your pieces from the cárcel with a pair of dice, spend each die on the piece you choose, hide on seguros, build barriers and send rivals back to jail. Play 1-3 computer opponents or pass one phone around the table, get hints, or watch a whole game with Auto Play.
howToPlay: Roll two dice: tap or swipe the tray.
Only a pair frees a piece from the cárcel onto your salida.
Each die is its own move: pick a die, then a glowing piece.
Land exactly on a rival outside a safe square to send it to jail.
Two of your pieces on one square form a barrier rivals cannot pass.
Bring all four pieces up your lane to the corona to win.

title: Pelota Vasca
tagline: Hit the wall. Read the angles. Win to 22.
description: The fast wall ball of the Basque Country in real 3D. Play one on one or two on two with the bare hand or a paddle, aim at the front and left walls, and time your swing. Five rivals, Learn lessons, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Drag to run, or let Auto-run take you to the ball.
Tap the wall to aim; choose Drive, Drop or Lob.
Press SWING when the ring closes around the button.
Use the left wall and the rebote; the ball may bounce once.
Win to 22 against five rival levels.

title: Perch
tagline: Read the stone. Choose your moment.
description: You are a small bird on a branch, and hunters with catapults ring the field. You never aim: you read the stone coming and choose your moment to fly. Survive each day until sunset for up to three stars. Level 1 is one tree; from level 2 whole groves and orchards open up and you choose where to fly. Every level adds one new idea: golden seeds, fast archers, wind, a Master Hunter with a pattern to learn, nets and beaters. From level 3, close calls earn acorns to knock hunters flat. A hit only ruffles feathers. No ads, works offline. An in-game Rules page covers every mechanic in detail.
howToPlay: A hunter pulls back a catapult and a red ring shows the perch the stone will hit. A dotted arc shows its path.
Level 1: tap anywhere to fly and the bird picks the safest perch. From level 2, tap the perch you want to fly to.
Leave at the last moment for a close call (+5). Dodges in a row build a combo up to x5.
You have 3 feathers. Survive until the bar at the top fills (sunset): 3 stars for no hits.
Golden seeds: tap the perch that holds one to fly for it. Every third seed heals a feather.
Archers fire fast arrows. In wind, trust the red ring, not the hunter. Nets cover a whole tree: leave it. Beaters rattle your perch.
Hit back (level 3+): close calls earn acorns, up to 3. Tap a hunter to knock him down and cancel his shot.
Boss levels: the Master Hunter fires the same pattern every attempt. Learn it.

title: The Royal Game of Ur
tagline: A race from the cradle of civilisation
description: The Royal Game of Ur is the Game of Twenty Squares, played in Mesopotamia over four thousand years ago. Roll four pyramid dice and race seven inlaid pieces down your lane, up the shared middle lane and home. Rosettes are safe and give another roll; landing on an enemy sends it back. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, watch Auto Play demonstrate a whole game move by move at your own pace, play four computer levels or a friend, and solve a daily best-move puzzle. Lapis, shell and red-limestone art lit by an oil lamp. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
Tap the dice to roll four pyramid dice: each gold tip up counts 1, so a roll is 0 to 4.
Tap a glowing piece, then the glowing square it goes to. Moves are exact.
Your path: 4 squares in your lane, 8 in the shared middle lane, then 2 home. Rosettes give another roll.
Landing on an enemy piece in the middle lane sends it back. A piece on a rosette is safe.
The central rosette blocks the lane: nobody can land there while it is occupied.
A piece leaves the board only with the exact roll. First to bring all seven home wins.
Refused move? The piece tries and returns, and a message says why. Hints and Take back help.

title: Sapo: Frog Toss
tagline: Toss brass discs at the open mouth of the frog.
description: The classic tavern table game of Peru, Chile and Argentina. Pull back, aim, add spin and drop brass discs into the golden frog's mouth for 500.
howToPlay: Drag down in the lower part of the screen to pull the disc back; the ring shows where it lands.
Pick a high Lob or a low Drive, and a spin to the left or right.
A disc that drops into a hole scores: the frog's mouth is worth 500.
Loose discs stay on the table: knock your rival's away.
After each round the loose disc nearest the mouth earns a bonus. Tap Think for a tested throw.

title: Scopa
tagline: The Italian card game of the broom
description: Scopa is one of Italy's three major national card games, played with a 40-card Italian deck: coins, cups, swords and batons. Match a card's rank or a sum to capture it, clear the table for a scopa, and score cards, coins, sette bello and primiera. Nine hands-on lessons, free Auto Play at your own pace, four computer levels to a card-counting Maestro, four-player partnerships, and a new daily deal every day. Original hand-drawn Italian court cards, a trattoria table, and a French-suit option. No ads, no chips, score only.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP a card in your hand, then TAP a table card of the same rank to capture it.
If several table cards add up to your card's rank, TAP each one to take the whole set.
A matching card must always be taken alone, even when a sum is also possible.
Clear the table and you score a scopa: one point, shown with a flourish (not on the round's last play).
Nothing to capture? TAP your card again to lay it on the table.
A round is scored on most cards, most coins, the sette bello and primiera. Play to 11 or 21.
Daily deal: find the single most valuable capture. Same deal for everyone, every day.

title: Seega: Desert Siege
tagline: Place. Slide. Sandwich.
description: A traditional Egyptian board game for a 5x5 board, made beautiful. Fill the board two stones at a time, leaving only the centre empty, then slide your stones and trap enemy stones between two of yours. Lit pebbles and date stones sit on a carved sandstone board. Five opponent levels from Novice to Master, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, a short Learn course and Watch & Learn. Play in English or in Arabic. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has 12 stones. Take turns placing two stones at a time on any empty square except the centre, until the board is full.
Then slide one stone a step, up, down, left or right, into an empty square. The side that placed last moves first, into the centre.
Trap an enemy stone between two of yours, in a row or column, to capture it. One slide can take several; the same stone may go on.
Corners can never be captured and the centre square is safe too. If a side cannot move, the other side moves again.
Reduce your opponent to one stone to win. Think shows a good move and why; Learn and Watch & Learn teach the ideas.

title: Senet
tagline: The board game of ancient Egypt
description: Senet is the board game of ancient Egypt, played for thousands of years and shown in tomb paintings. Throw four sticks, race five pieces along a 30-square path, swap lone enemy pieces, hold a wall of three, and avoid the House of Water. Rules follow a widely published modern reconstruction. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace, play five computer levels or a friend, and solve a daily puzzle. Ebony-and-ivory board, gilded inlay, faience pieces, tumbling sticks. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Ten short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP the sticks to throw. Count the light faces: 1 to 4, or 5 if none. A 1, 4 or 5 earns another throw.
TAP a glowing piece, then TAP a glowing square. It moves exactly the number thrown, along the S-shaped path.
Land on a lone enemy piece to swap places. Pairs, and pieces on safe houses, cannot be swapped.
Three pieces in a row make a wall that nothing can pass. Every piece must stop on square 26.
Square 27 is the House of Water: it sends a piece back to 15. Leave with exact throws: 5 from 26, 3, 2 or 1 from 28-30.
A refused move shakes and tells you why. Hint shows a good move; Take back undoes yours.
First to bring all five pieces home wins. Beat each level for a star; a new puzzle every day.

title: Sepak Takraw
tagline: Receive. Set. Scissor-kick it over the net.
description: Lead a team of three in sepak takraw, the acrobatic kick-volleyball of Southeast Asia, in real 3D. Choose your receive, your set and your attack, time the kick, and read the block. Five rival teams, a Learn path, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Tap the court to aim, choose a serve and press SERVE when the ring closes.
Choose which player attacks, then where and how the set goes.
Pick an attack and press SMASH on the ring: roll, sunback, scissor, header or foot.
Choose a single block, a double block or drop back when they set.
Win two sets out of three to 21.

title: Shagai
tagline: Toss four ankle bones, hold the best, gallop the felt trail
description: A dice race inspired by the ankle-bone games of Mongolia. Toss four bones that land as Horse, Camel, Sheep or Goat, hold the ones you like and toss the rest again, then gallop your bone-horse along a winding trail across the steppe. Land on a tailwind, avoid marmot burrows, and flick rivals back. Play one to three computer riders, get Hints, or watch a whole race with Auto Play.
howToPlay: Tap or swipe up on the felt mat to toss four bones.
Each side is worth strides; matching sides earn a bonus.
Tap bones to hold them, then Toss again (up to two more times).
Press Gallop: your bone-horse rides that many stations.
Tailwinds push you on, burrows push you back, and landing on a rival flicks them back.
First to station 66 wins.

title: Shogi
tagline: Japan's game of generals and drops
description: Shogi is the chess-like strategy game of Japan, played on a 9 by 9 board. Its big idea: a captured piece changes sides and can be dropped back on any empty point. Learn in twelve hands-on lessons where you make every move, play five computer levels from Novice to Master as either side, try the quick 5x5 mini board, or pass the phone to a friend. Every refused move is explained, hints tell you why, and a new checkmate puzzle arrives every day. Hand-drawn kaya board and boxwood pieces, large text and reduced motion options. No ads, works offline. Play in 日本語 or English. Full rules built in.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: twelve short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP one of your pieces: every point it may move to glows. TAP a glowing point to move.
Landing on an enemy piece captures it. Captured pieces wait on your stand under the board.
To drop: TAP a piece on your stand, then TAP an empty glowing point.
Reach the last three rows and you may promote: TAP Promote or Keep.
Not allowed? The piece tries and returns, and a message says why (check, nifu, blocked...).
Win by checkmate. Hint (3 per game) and Take back help you learn.
The puzzle of the day is mate in 1 on weekdays and mate in 3 at the weekend.

title: Snooker: Cue and Frame
tagline: Pot, spin, build the break.
description: Snooker on a fixed table with real ball physics: top spin, back spin, side spin, cushions and pockets. Aim, pull the cue back, pot a red and a colour, and build a break. Play five computer opponents, share the phone, learn the shots in short lessons, or watch two players explain their choices.
howToPlay: Drag on the table to aim; drag in the Fine aim window for small turns.
Drag on the white ball circle to choose top spin, back spin or side spin.
Pull the cue back on the Power strip and let go to shoot.
Pot a red (1 point), then a colour (2 to 7), and keep going; when the reds are gone, pot the colours in order.
A foul gives the other player at least 4 points.

title: Spinning Tops Arena
tagline: Wind it. Launch it. Last one spinning wins.
description: A physics duel with turned wooden tops in a lacquered dish. Build your top in the workshop, pull the cord, whip it to speed and watch the spin, the wobble and the clash decide it. Five rivals, three dishes, two players on one device.
howToPlay: Build a top: body, tip, rim weight, spin direction.
Press near your top and drag back, then let go.
Tap when the needle is in the gold to whip the cord.
Watch the clash: a slow top wobbles, a hard hit near the rim sends a top out.
Win two rounds out of three.

title: Surakarta
tagline: The looping capture game
description: A Javanese-named strategy game on a carved board of looping tracks. Pieces step one point but capture by racing round the circuits and the corner loops, with every legal route drawn as a glowing trail. Five opponent levels, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, seven lessons and Watch & Learn. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has 12 pieces. Light plays from the bottom and moves first. Capture every enemy piece to win.
Tap a piece, then a free neighbouring point to step one point in any direction.
To capture, select a piece: glowing trails show routes along the circuits, round a corner loop. Tap the piece at the end of one.
A capturing piece may pass over its own starting point, so even a neighbouring enemy can be taken the long way round.
Think shows the best move and why. The eye button rings pieces that can be captured next turn.
Learn teaches loops, circuits, defence and clean captures. Watch & Learn plays a whole game with a Pause button.

title: Sure Sweep
tagline: No-guess minesweeper. Every board solves by logic alone.
description: Sure Sweep is classic mine-clearing with one guarantee: every board can be fully solved by logic, with no lucky guesses required. Tap to reveal, flip the switch to flag suspected mines, and chord through satisfied numbers to clear the board fast. Stuck? A free hint shows you the deduction you missed, and one free Undo takes back a fatal tap. Sea-chart art, a calm teal palette, and colour schemes you can switch anytime. A full in-app Rules page covers every mechanic.
howToPlay: Tap a cell to reveal it.
A number shows how many mines touch that cell.
Flip the Reveal/Flag switch to Flag, then tap a cell to mark it as a suspected mine.
Tap a revealed number when its flags match it to clear the safe cells around it.
Reveal every non-mine cell to win - the board is guaranteed solvable without guessing.
Stuck? Tap Hint for a free forced move while you play.
Lose a board? Tap Undo once to take back the fatal tap and keep going.
Tap the colour button on the title screen or while playing to switch colour schemes - your choice is remembered.

title: Tab: Stick Race
tagline: The four-stick race of Egypt and the Arab world
description: A traditional race-and-capture game played with four tumbling throwing sticks. Bring your stones on with a one, slide them along a carved 28-square path, land on your rival's stones, rest on the star squares and be first home. Five opponent levels, two players on one phone, Think that explains moves with the real chances of the next throws, a Learn course and Watch & Learn. Play in English or Arabic. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has seven stones (or four in a quick game). Bring every stone home before your rival does.
Tap Throw: four sticks tumble. Flat sides up are your count: none flat is 6, one is 1, two is 2, three is 3, four is 4.
After a 1, 4 or 6 you throw again. A 2 or 3 ends your throws. Keep every count and spend them in any order.
A 1 brings a stone on. Spend a count: tap a stone, then the glowing square. Landing on a rival stone captures it.
A stone on a star square cannot be captured. A stone carried past the last square goes home.
Think shows the best move and why. Learn teaches the rules. Watch & Learn plays a whole game with a Pause button.

title: Tangram: Seven Pieces
tagline: Seven pieces. Endless shapes.
description: The classic Chinese seven-piece puzzle, made to feel wonderful. Drag, turn, flip and click the pieces into more than 80 hand-checked silhouettes, from animals and people to the thirteen convex shapes. A Daily Puzzle, stars, a hint that teaches, and Watch & Learn, which solves a puzzle step by step. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Fill the dark silhouette with all seven pieces. Pieces may not overlap or leave gaps.
Drag a piece with one finger. Let go near a corner and it clicks into place.
Tap a piece to select it, tap again to turn it 45 degrees, or drag the round handle.
The parallelogram is the only piece that needs flipping: select it and press Flip.
Press Hint to see which piece goes where, press again to have it placed.
Three stars for no hints. Solve eight puzzles in a chapter to open the next.
Watch & Learn plays a puzzle for you, step by step, with time to think.

title: Tarneeb
tagline: The partnership card game of the Levant
description: Tarneeb is the bidding-and-trump trick-taking card game of the Levant. You and a computer partner bid against two computer opponents for how many of 13 tricks your side will take; the winning bidder names trump and leads. Follow suit, take tricks, and score by what you win. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, play four computer levels with hints that explain the reasoning, and solve a new open-hand Daily Deal every day. An in-app Rules page covers bidding and scoring in full. Designed cards with a large-print option, a warm cafe table. No ads, offline, score only.
howToPlay: Four players, two partnerships: you and your partner against two computer opponents.
Bidding: each player bids 7 to 13 tricks or passes. High bidder names trump and leads.
TAP a card to lift it, TAP again (or DRAG it up) to play. You must follow the suit led.
Highest trump wins a trick; with no trump played, highest card of the suit led wins.
Make your bid and your side scores its tricks; fall short and your side loses the bid.
Eight lessons teach following suit, trump, bidding, partnership play and a full hand.
Daily Deal: all hands face up. Only one first card can reach the target; find it, then play it out.
Hint explains a good bid or card with a reason; Undo takes back your last move.

title: Tavla
tagline: The dice game of the coffeehouse
description: Tavla is backgammon as played in the coffeehouses of Turkey, the Arab world, Israel and Persia, also called tawla, shesh besh and takhteh nard. Race fifteen checkers around 24 points, hit lone checkers, build walls and bear off first. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new best-move puzzle every day. Hints explain why, undo is one tap, forced moves can play themselves. Optional score-only doubling cube and gammons. Inlaid wooden board, carved checkers, tumbling dice. Large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
